advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make first_pass_verification skip gate_error_v1 (non-verdict) records when finding a ticket's earliest completion verdict, per its own docstring.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:222-223: `it counts toward the numerator when its oldest such record (by filename/chronological order) is a completion_verifier_pass_v1`
src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:22-24: `A gate_error_v1 record ... rides on the REVIEW_RESULT stream ... or the COMPLETION_VERDICT stream (completion gate)`
advisory.finding: first_pass_verification counts the earliest COMPLETION_VERDICT-stream *record*, but per this module's own docstring a gate_error_v1 ERROR rides on the COMPLETION_VERDICT stream for the completion gate; when a ticket's earliest in-range completion-stream record is such an ERROR, the ticket is added to the denominator with earliest_schema='gate_error_v1' (never the numerator), contradicting the documented 'earliest completion verdict is a pass' semantics and understating the first-pass rate.
scenarios: A ticket whose first completion-stream event is a gate_error_v1 ERROR (an infra/gate error) rather than a pass/fail verdict
advisory.suggested_fix: In the loop, continue past records where schema == _GATE_ERROR (or verdict not in {PASS,FAIL}) before assigning earliest_schema/breaking, so only true completion verdicts define the earliest verdict.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/document whether the closing same-gate PASS must be in-range; if the ERROR anchors the interval, don't range-filter the PASS.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:167-174: `_next_same_gate_pass` calls `_in_range(ts, lo, hi)` and returns None when the PASS is out of range

src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:32-33: docstring only promises pairing with 'the next same-gate PASS', and 'An ERROR with no following same-gate PASS is omitted' — no mention of range-clipping the PASS
advisory.finding: env_diagnosis_intervals requires the closing same-gate PASS to itself fall within [since,until); an in-range ERROR whose next same-gate PASS lands after `until` (or before `since`) is silently dropped, so a range boundary can hide an otherwise-complete diagnosis interval — a behavior the docstring never states (it only says an ERROR with no following same-gate PASS is omitted).
scenarios: A gate ERROR near the end of the requested window whose recovery PASS occurs just after `until`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a first_pass_verification test where a ticket's earliest completion-stream record is a gate_error_v1 ERROR.
evidence: tests/unit/metrics/test_sidecar_metrics_heldout.py:_completion only writes completion_verifier_pass_v1 / completion_verifier_fail_v1 schemas; no gate_error_v1 on the COMPLETION_VERDICT stream is exercised
ABSENCE: no test writes a completion-stream gate_error_v1 as a ticket's earliest completion record
advisory.finding: Held-out tests do not cover the documented gate_error_v1-on-COMPLETION_VERDICT-stream case for first_pass_verification, leaving the earliest-verdict-vs-earliest-record ambiguity unpinned.
scenarios: Regression where a completion-stream gate error is (mis)counted as a first-pass denominator entry

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a cost_per_accepted_change case with >1 accepted completion pass so the /accepted division is exercised.
evidence: test asserts `cost_per_accepted_change(str(tmp_path)) == 9.0  # 9 llm_calls / 1 accepted` — denominator is 1
held-out `test_cost_reads_review_metrics_only` also uses a single accepted close: `assert cost_per_accepted_change(str(tmp_path)) == 5.0`
src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:130-133 `if accepted == 0: return None; return total_calls / accepted` — the /accepted step with accepted>1 is untested
advisory.finding: cost_per_accepted_change is only ever tested with exactly one accepted completion pass, so the per-accepted division (denominator > 1) is never exercised; a regression that dropped the division by `accepted` (returning the raw total, or mis-counting accepted closes) would still pass every test.
scenarios: A ticket (or tickets) with multiple completion_verifier_pass_v1 closes where the metric must divide total llm_calls by the count of accepted closes
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test with e.g. total llm_calls 10 over 2 completion_verifier_pass_v1 closes and assert the result == 5.0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test passing since/until bounds that includes some records and excludes others, asserting out-of-range records are dropped.
evidence: Every test call passes only repo_root, e.g. `cost_per_accepted_change(str(tmp_path))`, `env_diagnosis_intervals(str(tmp_path))`, `first_pass_verification(str(tmp_path))` — no since/until argument anywhere
src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:119 `if not _in_range(event.get("timestamp"), lo, hi): continue` (and 127, plus env/first_pass) gate on range but no test provides bounds
advisory.finding: No test exercises the since/until range filtering for any sidecar derivation, even though all three call _in_range on record timestamps and expose since/until as documented public parameters; a regression removing or inverting the range guard would not be caught.
scenarios: A since/until window that includes some records and excludes others across REVIEW_RESULT and COMPLETION_VERDICT streams
advisory.suggested_fix: Write records at distinct timestamps and assert cost/env/first-pass values change when since/until narrow the window.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a gate_error_v1 ERROR and no following same-gate PASS, asserting env_diagnosis_intervals returns no interval for it.
evidence: Both env tests supply a closing PASS; neither leaves an ERROR unpaired
src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:160-161 `if pass_ts is None or not isinstance(err_ts, int): continue` — the None-pass omission path has no test
advisory.finding: env_diagnosis_intervals's documented 'ERROR with no following same-gate PASS is omitted' branch is untested; a regression that emitted a spurious/partial interval for a dangling ERROR would pass.
scenarios: A gate_error_v1 ERROR with no subsequent same-gate PASS on the ticket
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a lone plan_review ERROR (no later plan_review PASS) and assert env_diagnosis_intervals(...) == [].
